surfaces.part: hearth top: coal bed seen from above inside a stone rim

answer.evidence: The main body is the stone hearth (rows 34-61, width 38-46). Rows 34-45 show a top: a stone rim around an open bed of glowing coals (rows 36-43, evidence d). The top ends in a dark front-edge line at row 46. Below it is a stone front face with a fire arch, rows 47-61 (15 rows). The chimney (rows 16-33) is a vertical stone face with only a 2-row dark cap at the top, so it has no real top surface. The wooden stair at the left is a side profile.

styleAnswer.evidence: Tile density is fine: 17 visible tones per tile matches the cheese stall (17) and sits just under the roofed well (20), and near-flat coverage is only 2%. The fire and coals have a decent orange gradient, and the chimney bricks are drawn individually. The weak point is the outline. 92% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, whereas the tinted-outline references measure 0-1% (hedge, cheese stall). The dark line around the chimney, hearth body and wood steps reads as a uniform neutral dark contour, which is the sticker look. It is not the dark brown, red-brown or green of the adjacent material that Beodeul uses. The grey stone ramp has about 4 steps, fewer than the 5-6 on the references' wood and tile. The steps and the smoke wisp are thin and simple. Because the outline is near-black and the shading is a little shallow, this fails the Beodeul bar.

answer.evidence: The main hearth body (rows 34-61) has an open top, rows 34-45, with glowing coals visible inside a stone rim (evidence d). A dark front-edge line at row 46 follows it. Below is a stone front face of rows 47-61 with an arched fire opening and a dark base. The chimney above is a vertical stack with a dark flue top at rows 16-18, and the smoke is decor. The wooden stair at the left is a small side detail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 17 visible tones per tile, level with the cheese stall (17) and close to the well (20). Near-flat coverage is only 2%, against 13% for the stall, so there are no flat fills. The chimney and hearth stones are shaded block by block with light, mid and dark steps, and the fire mouth has a graded ramp from white-yellow through orange to deep red. Embers and speckles add grain, and the stair and wood side has its own tones. The 92% near-neutral dark edge share is the main risk for a sticker look. But the outline mostly sits next to grey stone, where a dark grey edge is the material's own dark tone. The lamp-crook reference is 100% neutral for the same reason, and the fire opening and wood edges look more brown-black. I call the outline mixed, not a uniform black sticker line, and the piece sits at the reference level on density and shading.

answer.evidence: The main body is the wide hearth (rows 34-61). Rows 34-45 show an open trough filled with glowing coal and ember pixels inside a grey rim, so contents are visible from above (evidence d). The top ends in a dark front-edge line at row 46. Below it is a stone front face of about 15 rows (rows 47-61) with a fire arch and a dark base. The chimney (rows 16-33) is drawn only as a vertical brick face with a thin 2-row dark flue cap, and the side steps are also vertical, so not every part has a top surface. The main body still reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 17 visible tones per tile, matching the cheese stall (17) and close to the well (20). Near-flat coverage is 2%, so there are no big flat fills. The stone chimney has brick-by-brick shading, and the fire mouth and ember bed have a warm gradient. Structure and density are fine. The outline is the weak point: 92% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral. That is the same neutral-black line seen on the lamp, whereas the richer references (hedge 0%, stall 1%, well 33%) use tinted dark material tones. The dark outline around the chimney, hearth body and wood stack reads as a uniform near-black sticker line instead of dark stone, brown or red tones. This breaks the Beodeul outline rule, so the piece fails on outline despite adequate shading and density.

answer.evidence: Main body spans rows 34-61. Rows 34-45 form a wide top opening filled with glowing embers and coals (evidence d), bounded by a stone rim. Row 46 is a dark front-edge line, and below it the stone front face runs rows 47-61 (15 rows) with a fire arch and a dark base. The chimney on top has a dark opening at rows 16-18. The wooden stair at the left is a small side attachment. Silhouette widths (39 then 46) show the broad top with the face below it.

styleAnswer.evidence: Density is fine: 17 visible tones per tile matches the cheese stall (17) and is close to the roofed well (20), and near-flat coverage is only 2%. The fire mouth and ember bed show several orange and yellow steps, and the chimney stonework has some brick variation. The weaknesses are structural. About 92% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the dark line round the whole hearth reads as a near-black sticker outline. The references that carry colour (hedge 0%, cheese stall 1%) use tinted edges instead. The stone body is shaded in only about 4 steps, with little per-brick highlight or speckle compared with the 5-6 step ramps and per-tile detail on the well roof and stall awning. The wooden stair/rack on the left is thin and flat. Overall it is competent but shallower than the Beodeul standard on outline and stone shading.
